newsitem.title: USA: EU likely to give EMU fx method early - IMF official.
newsitem.headline: EU likely to give EMU fx method early - IMF official.

text.p: The European Union is likely to announce a method for fixing exchange rates among countries joining Economic and Monetary Union at the same time as they decide which countries qualify to join EMU in 1999, an IMF official said on Saturday.
"There are various alternatives which are being considered right now," Jacques Artus, deputy director of the IMF's European department, told a news conference.
"It will be likely that at the time you take the decision on membership that you announce the methodology," he said. "It will be useful to announce ahead of time how it will be done."
According to the Maastricht treaty, exchange rates between currencies joining monetary union cannot be fixed until the last day before the new euro is launched on January 1, 1999.

But some officials have suggested announcing early the method to be used in fixing exchange rates to head off market speculation between late April/early May 1998, when EU leaders will decide which countries can join a single currency, and its launch in January 1999.
"You can't leave the market without any information whatsoever. Then it would be chaos," Artus said.

He noted that there would be no macroeconomic variables on which the markets could make a decision about appropriate rates, since in theory, by then, all economies of countries joining EMU would have converged.

He made no comment on what method he thought should be used for fixing exchange rates, but noted that two ideas -- using central rates in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) or using an average of exchange rates over a period of time -- had been suggested.
Massimo Russo, special advisor on EMU issues to IMF managing director Michel Camdessus, also said he believed the EU would act to head off speculation on how exchange rates would be fixed.
"My understanding is that something will be done to address that issue," he said.
